title: Achilles tendinopathy
publisher: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust
claims: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS states Achilles tendinopathy is usually diagnosed from history and examination without X-ray or scans.
GSTT describes relative rest: reduce weight-bearing activity such as long walks or runs while continuing other exercise such as cycling or swimming.
GSTT early-stage heel-drop holds are 20 to 30 seconds repeated 3 times; later-stage raises are 10 to 12 repetitions repeated 3 times.
GSTT states most people need 6 to 9 months of rehabilitation before returning to full activity without pain, and flare-ups during recovery are normal.
GSTT lists sudden increases in activity, tight or weak calf muscles, stiff ankle joints, overweight, and too much hill running among contributing factors.

claimVerification.note: 原文：“You do not need an X-ray or other scans to diagnose Achilles tendinopathy. We usually confirm the diagnosis by asking about your medical history and examining you.”
原文 Relative rest 段：“reduce the activities you do on your feet, such as walking or running for a long time”；“keep fit by doing other types of exercise, such as cycling or swimming”。
原文 Exercise 1：“Hold this position for 20 to 30 seconds”“Repeat this exercise 3 times”；Exercise 3：“Do this 10 to 12 times”“repeat this exercise 3 times”。
原文：“Most people need 6 to 9 months of rehabilitation before they can return to full activities without pain”；“It is normal to have some periods of increased pain or flare-ups during your recovery.”
原文 contributing factors 列表含 a sudden increase in activity levels、tight or weak calf muscles、stiff ankle joints、being overweight，以及 training errors “too much hill running”。
